featured_reviews.review_text:
Dear Manager,

I am writing to express my disappointment with the recent customer service experience at your establishment. A few months ago, we purchased a gold chain from your store, which unfortunately broke. Instead of opting for a repair, we decided to exchange it for a new one.

As long-standing customers, we requested a reasonable accommodation—to pay half of the difference for the 14K gold (including GST) upfront, with the remaining amount to be settled by evening. This was due to a temporary cash shortage and the fact that our elderly parents, who were handling the transaction, are not well-versed with digital payment methods like GPay. Despite surrendering the old chain and assuring full payment by the end of the day, the executive on duty was uncooperative and insensitive to our situation.

It was disheartening to see a lack of empathy, especially toward senior citizens who had to make an additional trip due to this inflexibility. As a reputed jeweler, I expect your team to handle such situations with professionalism and courtesy, keeping in mind that customers may face genuine constraints.

Is this how you treat long-term customers? Earning commission doesn’t justify disrespect. Your staff should learn to be polite, humble, and understanding—especially toward seniors. If this is your standard of service, then BIG NO NEXT TIME.

I urge you to remind your staff to treat customers—especially elderly ones—with patience and understanding. A little compassion can go a long way in retaining trust and loyalty.

featured_reviews.name: Parag Murudkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Extremely low quoted valuations for their own gold jewellery and high making charges for the new ones, as compared to competition.
Not even bothered to verify their own jewellery pieces which needed to be exchanged for new ones. Valuation is probably done with zero consideration whether or not the old jewellery was made through them, by applying their standard valuation template to all and any.
What's more appalling is that they do not even take efforts to explain to the customer how the valuation breakup is structured.
It's a "take it or leave it" quote. Completely disappointed with the lack lustre attitude which really makes me sadly wonder that with today's cut throat competetion, how long before such businesses get relegated to the fringes???
featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text:
Dear Parag sir,

Thank you for taking the time to share your feedback. We’re genuinely sorry to hear that your recent experience did not meet your expectations.

We understand that gold exchange and valuation can feel complex and, at times, frustrating especially when the quoted value or making charges differ from what you anticipated. However, we would like to clarify that our valuation process is based on standardized industry parameters such as purity testing, net weight (excluding stones or impurities), and prevailing gold rates. These criteria are applied consistently to ensure fairness and transparency across all transactions, regardless of where the jewellery was originally purchased.

That said, we acknowledge your concern regarding the clarity of communication. We should have taken more time to walk you through the valuation breakdown in detail, including how deductions and making charges are calculated. This is valuable feedback, and we will certainly work with our team to improve how we explain these aspects to our customers.

Our goal is always to provide a transparent and respectful experience, and it’s disappointing to hear that we fell short in your case. 

Thank you again for your honest feedback it helps us improve.
